conceptZh: 玩具機器人面對一顆比他還大的飯糰，嘴巴張到不能再大、慢慢逼近，用力咬下去——結果只咬到一粒米；他把那粒米慢慢嚼完，認真地點點頭比出大拇指，好像剛吃完大餐。
object: a small toy robot and a rice ball bigger than he is
morph: the glyph 吃 stands still as a solid sculpture while the giant-bite gag plays out at its base
creativeAngle: 吃飯是每天都在用的字，笑點用「張最大的嘴、吃到最小的一口」的落差，再加上他一本正經的滿足反應，比單純咬一口有趣得多。吃為口部加乞共六畫，口部孩子已經學過可以互相連結，字體靜止保結構。語音詞「吃飯」，吃ㄔ、飯ㄈㄢˋ都是單一讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale mint background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 吃 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep pumpkin orange, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 口 radical on the left and the 乞 component on the right stay clearly separated, with the hook at the bottom of 乞 fully formed. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base stands a small boxy toy robot facing a glossy white rice ball noticeably bigger than he is. From 0.6 seconds his jaw hinges open, and open, and further open, until his mouth is comically wider than his own head. He shuffles towards the rice ball, closes his eyes, and at 2.0 seconds chomps down with total commitment. He pulls back. One single grain of rice is sitting on his tongue. Hold on that for a beat. At 2.9 seconds he begins to chew it with enormous care, eyes closed, savouring, taking far longer than one grain deserves. At 3.8 seconds he swallows, opens his eyes, gives a slow appreciative nod and a small thumbs-up to the untouched rice ball, then pats his tummy and walks out of frame to the right by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 吃 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「吃、吃、吃飯」, using the reading ㄔ for 吃 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 吃 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 吃飯 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 吃: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 豬探長衝太猛，飛過頭撞進米飯碗，滑回來後輕輕一口，咬出「吃」的左邊小嘴巴，再一口完成。
object: a stout detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat with a giant magnifying glass, a huge steaming rice bowl, and chunky orange-red strokes
morph: the pig overshoots a rice bowl, skids back, and on a gentle second try the rice-bowl mouth and its right part fall into the glyph 吃
creativeAngle: 衝過頭：豬探長餓到失控，飛過飯碗摔滑，第二次輕輕一口才成功；左邊的「口」就像他張大的嘴，呼應「吃飯」。
promptEn: An 8-second cheerful cartoon clip on a clean solid pale sage-cream backdrop. The only on-screen text is one large Traditional Chinese glyph 吃, built from thick glossy saturated vermilion-orange strokes, about 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped. Lead: a stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat, carrying a magnifying glass far too big for him; one supporting object, a huge steaming bowl of white rice with a pair of chopsticks. No background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Voice: warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin saying exactly 吃、吃、吃飯 (ㄔ、ㄔ、ㄔ ㄈㄢˋ), slowly with clear tones, then stop. Moment 1 (0–1.6s): the pig sniffs the rising steam, his nose stretching like a straw, then charges the bowl at full speed while the first 吃 is spoken, ears streaming back, the big magnifying glass dragging behind him. Moment 2 (1.6–3.2s): he flies right over the bowl, lands in a skid, spins twice on his belly, and slides all the way back to the starting spot with a cartoon squeak, hat spinning down over his eyes, while a square orange mouth shape pops out of the rice, drawn by the steam. Moment 3 (3.2–5s): a quiet beat, he adjusts his hat, takes a deep breath, and gently takes one tiny bite of rice; a ring of orange strokes pops out of the bowl, the small square mouth on the left forming with a click, and as the second 吃 is spoken the right part, a bent stroke with a hooked tail, slides in beside it to complete 吃. Moment 4 (5s): the word 吃飯 is spoken as he lifts the chopsticks and shovels a rice ball into his mouth in two quick cheek-bulging scoops, a few grains flicking into the air. Final 5–8s: the glyph 吃 stays perfectly still and fully legible, while the pig, sitting to one side, chews happily, pats his round belly, and wiggles his hat in a small drum-like rhythm without touching any stroke. Soft daylight, no flashing, no real people, no other writing.
